paper: Robinson, Nathaniel R. et al. 2024. "Kreyol-MT: Building MT for Latin American, Caribbean and Colonial African Creole Languages." arXiv:2405.05376.
license: MIXED, verified per-source rather than assumed for the whole pocket -- see license_verification below. The GitHub repository's own code/docs are MIT (repo/LICENSE, copied verbatim from the clone). The full aggregated bitext hosted on HuggingFace carries a top-level dataset license of "other" (not a recognized open license) and is NOT staged here for that reason. What IS staged is fetched directly from two independently-verified open upstream sources Kreyol-MT itself documents using: OPUS bible-uedin (CC0 1.0 Universal, per that package's own bundled LICENSE file) for djk-eng, and Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR by default, per Tatoeba's own terms of use) for hat-eng, gcf-fra, tpi-eng, crs-fra.

license_verification.method: git clone --depth 1 of the real JHU-CLSP/Kreyol-MT GitHub repository, then LICENSE and README.md read directly from the clone; every per-source README.md under data-documentation/ (344 files) grepped and sample-read directly (not summarized from memory); the live HuggingFace dataset card fetched via https://huggingface.co/datasets/jhu-clsp/kreyol-mt/raw/main/README.md and the HF datasets API (https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/jhu-clsp/kreyol-mt); the actual OPUS bible-uedin djk-en package downloaded and its bundled LICENSE file read directly; Tatoeba's live terms-of-use page fetched and read directly (https://tatoeba.org/en/terms_of_use#section-6).
license_verification.github_repo_finding: MIT License, stated in full in the repo's own LICENSE file. This governs the repository's code, scripts, and documentation only -- the repo contains no bitext data files itself.
license_verification.huggingface_dataset_finding: cardData license field is literally "other". The dataset card's own README states: "Documentation of all our data, including license and release information for data from individual sources, is available at our GitHub repo" -- i.e. the aggregate dataset explicitly defers to per-source licensing rather than asserting one license for itself. The card also states the currently-hosted parquet lacks per-row source metadata ("Metadata indicating which aligned sentences came from which sources" is listed as a future addition), so a downloaded parquet cannot be filtered to public-only sentences after the fact.
license_verification.per_source_documentation_finding: Across data-documentation/ (344 source READMEs, one per language-pair-source triple), grep of the 'release:' frontmatter field found 3 values: public (144), online (50), private (131). 'private' is dominated by a single source: 'JHU Bible' (112 of 344 entries, by far the largest single documented source in the whole project), plus CreoleVal (17) and AfricaNLP-2023 (2). The project's own scripts/count/count.py computes its 'public' sentence counts by checking release == 'public' exactly, meaning even the 'online' (OPUS-hosted) tier is excluded from what the project's own tooling treats as public data. Several 'public'-tagged sources still carry restrictive licenses when read individually, e.g. FLORES-200 is release:"public" but licensed CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 (noncommercial) per its own per-source README.
license_verification.decision: Because the HuggingFace-hosted bitext is an unlabeled blend of public/online/private-marked sentences with no license of its own and no way to separate a private-marked majority source after the fact, this pocket does NOT stage that blended data. Instead it fetches real bitext directly from two upstream sources Kreyol-MT's own documentation names as feeding several of its language pairs, at the point each source states its own clean license: OPUS bible-uedin (djk-en package's own LICENSE file: CC0 1.0 Universal) and Tatoeba (terms of use: CC BY 2.0 FR default for text sentences). Both confirmed independently, not inferred from Kreyol-MT's characterization of them.
license_verification.result: Clean, verified, per-source licenses for everything actually staged (CC0 for djk-eng; CC BY 2.0 FR for the four Tatoeba-built pairs; MIT for the repo/ code mirror). The much larger blended HuggingFace release is explicitly gated/skipped, named and reasoned about rather than silently omitted.

fetch_method: git clone --depth 1 of https://github.com/JHU-CLSP/Kreyol-MT.git for the repo's own LICENSE/README/data-documentation tree (used for verification, not as a bitext source); direct curl download of the real OPUS bible-uedin djk-en Moses-format package from https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-bible-uedin/v1/moses/djk-en.txt.zip (found via the live OPUS REST API at https://opus.nlpl.eu/opusapi/); direct curl download of Tatoeba's real per-language sentence exports and translation-link exports from https://downloads.tatoeba.org/exports/per_language/, joined locally by sentence ID into aligned bitext TSVs (join script logic: for each (src_id, tgt_id) pair in the *_links.tsv export, look up src_id in the source language's *_sentences.tsv and tgt_id in the target language's *_sentences.tsv; write the row only if both lookups succeed). No content was reconstructed from memory anywhere in this pocket.
coverage: A small, deliberately bounded, honestly partial slice: 5 of the ~74 language-pair configs Kreyol-MT tracks (and 5 of its ~40 target creole languages), chosen to span the three regional groups Kreyol-MT's own README organizes its target list into (African-diaspora Creoles of the Americas: djk, hat, gcf; Creoles of Africa/Indian Ocean: crs; other Creoles: tpi, Pacific) -- and chosen specifically because each is drawn from a source independently verified as openly licensed, not because it is a representative sample of Kreyol-MT's overall data composition (which is dominated by the private-marked JHU Bible source this pocket excludes). 18,163 real aligned sentence pairs total across the 5 pairs. Of Kreyol-MT's ~40 target creole languages, only 10 (hat, jam, pap, tpi, srn, mfe, gcf, crs, sag, lou) appear in Tatoeba's per-language export listing at all; of those, gcf/hat/tpi/crs had a usable (non-trivial) sentence count fetched. Only 1 Kreyol-MT language (djk) appears in OPUS bible-uedin's language list, checked directly against the live OPUS API's full bible-uedin language set.
